newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico parties call for anti-U.S. drug stance.
newsitem.headline: Mexico parties call for anti-U.S. drug stance.

text.p: Mexico's opposition parties on Friday urged President Ernesto Zedillo not to be cowed by the United States when Washington announces whether it will certify the country's anti-narcotics efforts this month.
"The government, particularly the president, has to take a stand...to defend the country's sovereignty," said Congressman Javier Gonzalez of the Party of the Democratic Revolution.

He and other lawmakers of Mexico's main leftist party held a news conference to denounce the controversial certification process, in which countries face U.S. economic and trade sanctions if they fail to make the grade in the war against drugs.

Mexico, which has always been certified for its war on drug traffickers, suffered a setback this week after its main anti-drug fighter, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, was jailed on charges of drug corruption.

President Bill Clinton called the corruption charges against him "deeply troubling" and said the extent of Mexican corruption evident in the charges against Gutierrez would be a "mixed factor" in determining whether Mexico was cooperating with the United States on drugs.
Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria, in Washington to deal with the fallout from the general's arrest, took aim at the certification policy on Friday, saying it "in fact inhibits cooperation."
On Friday, a spokesman for the Senate Foreign Relations Committee in Washington said bluntly Mexico should be decertified.

"Mexico should not accept interference (from the United States) in its national territory nor the certification that this country intends to do," two congressmen of the National Action Party, Mexico's main conservative opposition force, said in a statement.

Mexican politicians have long argued that fighting drugs should be a shared burden, with as much onus on the United States to stop consumption as there is on Latin American countries to stop production and trafficking.
